metaTitle: Clogged Drain Cleaning in Los Angeles, CA | Pricing & Info
metaDescription: Slow or blocked drain in your LA home? Learn common causes, what a plumber does, and the real cost ($135–$315) to get it cleared.
intro: A slow-draining sink or tub is one of the most common plumbing complaints in Los Angeles, whether you're in a pre-war bungalow with decades-old pipes or a new-build apartment with modern plumbing that's still prone to clogs. Left alone, a partial clog usually gets worse and can lead to backups or water damage. Here's what typically causes it and what it costs to fix in LA.
causes: Hair, soap scum, and grease build up inside pipes over time, especially in bathroom sinks and tubs.
Older homes in neighborhoods with pre-war bungalows often have original cast-iron or clay pipes that have narrowed or corroded inside.
Tree roots can infiltrate older sewer lines, particularly in areas with mature landscaping common around mid-century homes.
Food scraps, coffee grounds, or grease poured down kitchen sinks harden and trap other debris.
In newer apartment buildings, shared plumbing stacks can clog from a neighboring unit's waste, causing slow drains even if your own habits are fine.
whatProDoes: Inspects the fixture and asks about symptoms (slow drain, gurgling, bad smell) to locate the likely clog location.
Uses a mechanical drain snake or auger to physically break up or pull out the blockage.
For tougher or deeper clogs, may use a motorized drain machine that reaches further into the pipe.
Runs water through the line afterward to confirm the clog is cleared and drainage has returned to normal.
Checks nearby fixtures or the cleanout access to rule out a larger issue further down the line, such as a main sewer blockage.
diyOrPro: A simple slow drain in a bathroom sink or tub is often safe to try yourself with a plunger or a basic hand-held drain snake. If multiple fixtures are backing up at once, water is coming up from a floor drain, or you smell sewage, that points to a main line issue — stop and call a plumber, since forcing a clog in the wrong spot can cause a backup into your home.
